data.title: Hyperscale Data plans askROI subsidiary to go public
data.description:
• Hyperscale Data (GPUS)  said on Friday that it plans to take its askROI AI subsidiary public in Q2 or Q3 2027 through an IPO, reverse takeover, or SPAC transaction.

  • Joseph Spaziano is expected to become the askROI CEO, succeeding Milton “Todd” Ault III, while Ryan Doucette is expected to take over as President.

  • Spaziano, who serves as Hyperscale Data’s CTO and askROI’s president and COO, is expected to leave his parent-company role to focus on askROI.

  • A separate listing could give askROI an independent market valuation and provide Hyperscale Data shareholders with greater visibility into the subsidiary’s value

  • Share -6.41%

data.title: Gold’n Futures names Curtis Riou as CEO
data.description:
• Gold’n Futures Mineral (GFTRF) on Friday announced the appointment of Curtis Riou as chief executive officer, effective immediately, following the resignation of Khaled Hatabah.
  • Riou is a professional geoscientist with more than 25 years of experience in environmental consulting and resource development across Canada's oil, gas, and mining sectors. He serves as chief operating officer of Apex Exploration and is a co-founder of X-Terra Environmental Services, a First Nation–owned environmental consulting firm.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Twilio falls 11% on sector-wide selling
data.description:
Twilio (TWLO) shares tumbled almost 11% on Friday, ending at $244.37 and shedding $29.03 from the previous close. 

The slide came as technology shares saw notable pressure, with the technology sector ETF off just over 3% and the Nasdaq-tracking QQQ declining 2.5%. Several of Twilio's peers also moved lower, with Cloudflare falling more than 6%, Figma down more than 6%, and Applovin off nearly 5%.

Lately, the central debate among investors has centered on whether TWLO can sustain accelerating profit growth as AI agent-driven communications volumes rise, while managing competitive pressure from large cloud providers and the risk that carriers capture direct connectivity economics. Jefferies flagged those investor concerns on October 7, pointing specifically to the question of whether personal AI assistants can drive meaningful voice infrastructure demand ahead of earnings.

data.title: Palantir Technologies declines 7% amid broader tech selloff

Shares of the software and AI company, which serves government and commercial organizations, have now finished lower in five consecutive sessions, coming off a 52-week high of $212.94 set early this week. 

The decline came amid a broader technology sector selloff that weighed on the Nasdaq-100. The technology SPDR ETF fell just over 3% on the session. Among individual stocks, CRWV fell almost 12%, SMCI dropped nearly 10%, and ORCL declined almost 5%.

data.title: NXG Cushing Midstream Energy Fund to change name and broaden investment policy to energy infrastructure
data.description:
• The NXG Cushing Midstream Energy Fund (SRV) said on Friday that its name has been changed to The NXG Cushing Energy Infrastructure Fund.
  • As of December 18, 2026, the fund will invest at least 80% of its net assets, plus any borrowings for investment purposes, in a portfolio of energy infrastructure investments, moving away from midstream energy investments.
  • As of October 15, 2026, 90% of the fund's net assets, plus borrowings for investment purposes, consist of energy infrastructure investments, and therefore the fund does not anticipate that any changes in its investment approach or rebalancing of its portfolio will be required in connection with the name and policy change.
  • SRV will continue to invest no more than 25% of its total assets in securities of energy master limited partnerships that qualify as publicly traded partnerships under the Internal Revenue Code.
  • SRV +2.09% to $41.48 post-market.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: BUUU Group announces 10-for-1 forward share split
data.description:
• BUUU Group (BUUU) said on Friday it will implement a 10-for-1 forward split of the company's ordinary shares, effective October 26, 2026.
  • The share subdivision is intended to make the company's Class A ordinary shares more accessible to a broader base of investors and to enhance their trading liquidity, the company said.
  • In connection with the share split, the maximum number of shares the company is authorized to issue will increase proportionately from 500,000,000 shares of no par value, divided into 250,000,000 Class A ordinary shares and 250,000,000 Class B ordinary shares, to 5,000,000,000 shares of no par value, divided into 2,500,000,000 Class A ordinary shares and 2,500,000,000 Class B ordinary shares.
  • The rights and restrictions attached to each class of shares will remain unchanged as well as the shareholder's percentage ownership interest or voting power in the company. 
  • No fractional shares will result from the share subdivision, the company noted.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: FAA poised to approve Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week - Reuters
data.description:
The Federal Aviation Administration ‌is set to approve the long-delayed Boeing (BA) 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week after completing a key safety review, Reuters reported Friday.

In one of the last steps prior to final approval, the FAA and Boeing (BA) reportedly held a successful meeting Friday of the Type Certification Board, which is comprised of agency management team members.

Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for ~30% of Boeing's (BA) outstanding ​737 backlog, but numerous delays have helped European rival Airbus' A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market.

A glitch with the latest update ​of the 737 ⁠MAX's navigation software threatened to further delay certification when Boeing (BA) disclosed it last month, but the FAA determined it did not pose a safety concern and did not require a fix as ​a condition of certifying the plane.

Boeing (BA) is still working on certifying ​the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production and six years behind schedule.

data.title: LexinFintech Holdings receives Nasdaq notification
data.description:
• LexinFintech (LX) announced on Friday it received a Nasdaq deficiency notice for failing to meet the $1 minimum bid price requirement.
  • Nasdaq has given the company until April 12, 2027, to restore compliance with its $1 minimum bid price rule for 10 consecutive business days.
  • The company is considering corrective measures, including a potential ADS ratio adjustment, to avoid possible delisting.
  • Share -6.14%
